scope: LiveKit audio publication context adoption versus owned microphone processor
runtime_evidence: Frozen two-client diagnostics: published tracks live/enabled/unmuted and GCM enabled, but call pipeline registry unavailable; receiver decoded duration/energy0. Transport stabilizes with local SFU1.9.12; this does not establish working audio.
source_evidence: Installed SDK LocalParticipant.publishOrRepublishTrack calls track.setAudioContext(this.audioContext) for a LocalAudioTrack before publication.
Installed SDK LocalAudioTrack.setAudioContext tears down an attached processor when a changed context becomes undefined.

HiChat MicrophoneTrackProcessor assigns an owned context to the track; Room may have undefined context. A focused regression using actual LocalAudioTrack, actual processor and actual pipeline registry reproduces ready state with missing registry when publication faithfully adopts the undefined SDK context.

Simply removing the track context assignment is invalid: installed LocalAudioTrack.setProcessor explicitly requires an audio context before invoking processor.init. This candidate was rejected before production source changes.
constraints_for_fix: Respect actual SDK public lifecycle contracts, including publish/re-publish and reconnect.
Never publish unprocessed enabled raw capture as a fallback; preserve current auth, call and encryption admission fences.
Preserve concurrent audio-startup hotfix changes and test both processor initialization and SDK publication context adoption with real classes.
After correction, repeat frozen two-client tests and require decoded duration/energy or audible evidence; packet bytes alone do not satisfy acceptance.
